sections.theory:
Newton’s laws of Motion

Newton’s laws related to motion have a basic status in present physical science. These laws are as follows.

First law of Motion

In the absence of any external force, a stationary body always remains at rest, and a moving body continues its motion with uniform speed in a straight line. This law is also called the law of inertia.

Second law of Motion

When some external force acts on some body, it produces acceleration in that body in its own direction. The magnitude of this acceleration is directly proportional to the external force and inversely proportional to the mass.

Third law of Motion

Every action of force has a reaction. Action and reaction are equal to each other but in opposite directions.

Equilibrium

When several forces act on a body at the same time and that body does not change its state of rest or state of motion, then this state of the body is called the state of equilibrium.

Centre of Gravity

In every body there is a special point where the whole weight of the body acts. This is called the centre of gravity.
